description: Machine-readable live work queue. Passing entries are retained for 24 hours, then removed by pnpm features:prune; durable behavior and evidence remain in product specs and Git/PR history. See docs/FEATURES.md for rules.

features.behavior: Each table gains a Structure view alongside Rows per docs/product-specs/schema-editing.md: columns listed with add/rename/drop/alter controls (capability-gated; hidden where the adapter reports not-applicable, e.g. MongoDB columns), index management (F112), and rename/truncate/drop-table actions behind the spec's typed confirmations - every action previews its DDL/ops first and surfaces the audit outcome. Views/matviews (F124) get the Structure information read-only with zero mutation affordances and their kind stated; read-only sessions likewise see structure info only (a strict improvement to today's read-only experience). E2E covers a column-add + index-create + drop-table roundtrip on one SQL engine, and the F097 read-only guard stays green. Depends on F111, F112, F113.

features.evidence: PR #130 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/130), merged as dd707f4. A Rows/Structure toggle on the Tables tab (useTableView, localStorage-backed like the Schema tab's graph/grid choice, surviving TablesTab's remount-on-table-switch). packages/ui's new TableStructure lists columns with Edit/Drop controls (EditColumnDialog combines rename+alter into one PATCH per F111's route shape; the new shared ConfirmTypedNameDialog primitive backs all three typed-confirmation flows: dropColumn/truncateTable/dropTable), an AddColumnDialog, indexes with an immediate Drop button (no confirmation - an index carries no user data, per the spec) plus CreateIndexDialog, and table-lifecycle actions (inline rename; typed-confirm Truncate/Drop table). Three independent gates via computeTableStructureEditability: canEditColumns (supportsDdl, false for MongoDB), canManageIndexes (supportsIndexManagement), canEditTable (supportsDdl); views/matviews or zero-capability sessions render the read-only TableDetail - zero write affordances, not disabled ones. e2e/read-only-mode.spec.ts's F097 guard extended to visit the Structure view and its button-name regex covers the new DDL control names. Found and fixed a real latent bug: dropTable/dropColumn/dropIndex (F110-F112) reply 204 No Content but the shared fetchJson helper unconditionally parsed a JSON body, throwing on the empty response (silently swallowed by the caller) - no UI had called those DELETE routes before F114; fixed fetchJson to return null on 204, covered by new fetch-json.test.ts. 36 new tests across packages/ui (ConfirmTypedNameDialog/AddColumnDialog/EditColumnDialog/CreateIndexDialog/TableStructure render tests) and apps/web (structure-editability, fetch-json, workspace-state reducer actions tableRenamed/tableDropped). Verified: pnpm check:quiet:run and pnpm verify:pr all green (CI also green on PR #130), plus manual browser verification of all 8 operations end-to-end against a live Postgres connection, including re-verifying dropIndex/dropColumn after the 204 fix.

features.behavior: Database/schema lifecycle where the engine supports it: adapters gain the admin namespace with listDatabases (Postgres/MySQL/MongoDB; SQLite not-applicable - one file is one database and must report that cleanly), createDatabase/dropDatabase, and Postgres schema create/drop; capabilities report supportsDatabaseManagement from the real F092-F095 introspection. Server routes gated + audited; drop requires the typed-confirmation token server-side. Conformance: list/create/drop roundtrip on the three applicable engines, restricted-user rejection, SQLite clean not-applicable. Needs a short spec section added to docs/product-specs/permissions-and-capabilities.md or schema-editing.md (decide during implementation, following F109's patterns). Depends on F096, F110.

features.evidence: PR #131 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/131), merged as 8ba44c3. Adapters gain the DatabaseAdminApi admin namespace (mirroring mutations/ddl's optional-namespace pattern): Postgres gets listDatabases/createDatabase/dropDatabase plus createSchema/dropSchema (no CASCADE on drop - a non-empty schema surfaces Postgres's own dependency error rather than silently taking every contained table with it, confirmed live); MySQL the database trio only (its "schema" IS its database); MongoDB listDatabases/dropDatabase only (databases exist implicitly on first write, so there is no create to model - the route responds 400 explaining that); SQLite has no namespace at all (one file is one database, routes reply a clean 400, never a bare 404). supportsDatabaseManagement was already introspected for real on Postgres (CREATEDB/superuser) and MySQL (global CREATE/SUPER) from F092/F093; MongoDB now derives it from the dropDatabase privilege action (the only database-management action its privilege model has), replacing its F095 always-false placeholder incl. the unauthenticated full-access default. New routes: GET /api/databases (a read, no gate), POST /api/databases, DELETE /api/databases/:database, POST /api/schemas, DELETE /api/schemas/:schema - mutating routes two-tier gated (F096 + supportsDatabaseManagement), both drops behind server-side typed confirmation, all audited with operation+target structured fields. Design decision documented in the spec's new "Database and schema lifecycle" section: DELETE /api/schemas/:schema deliberately has no exists-first 404, since getOverview() derives schemas from tables and an empty schema never appears in it. MongoDB's WRITE_METHODS lint-scan gained admin.ts as a third trusted write-path file. Verified: 16 new server route tests, 4 new conformance tests (create/list/drop roundtrip on Postgres/MySQL/MongoDB incl. MongoDB's implicit-creation path, SQLite absent-namespace, Postgres schema roundtrip, capability reporting), restricted-role rejection tests for Postgres/MySQL, updated MongoDB permission-shape unit tests - all green against live databases, pnpm check:quiet:run and pnpm verify:pr all green.

features.behavior: Database-level management UI: the connection/database switcher (F064/F085 flow) lists databases on the current server with switch-in-place, permission-gated create-database (name plus minimal engine-appropriate options), and drop-database behind typed confirmation; Postgres schema create/drop appears in the sidebar. Read-only or ungranted sessions see the list only, with the affordances hidden and the reason available. Depends on F115.
features.evidence: PR #132 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/132), merged as 94987a4. Shared DatabasePanel, CreateNamedDialog, and typed-confirmation patterns cover the UI. Verified live against Postgres for create/switch/drop database and schema dependency handling; 36 new/updated unit tests, pnpm check:quiet:run, full E2E, and both CI jobs passed.

features.behavior: Permission-gated CSV import into an existing table: a server endpoint streams and parses the upload (with an explicit request-size/row-count cap and multipart limits so a huge or malicious file cannot exhaust memory or disk - the F066 streaming-export philosophy in reverse), validates and coerces values per column type against introspected metadata, and inserts in bounded batches through the mutations namespace (transactional per batch, per-row error report with line numbers); the UI wizard maps CSV columns to table columns with a dry-run preview of the first rows and a clear success/failure summary. Kind-gated (tables/collections only) and permission-gated. Needs a short product-spec pass (docs/product-specs/csv-import.md) before implementation, following the F063-F066 pattern. Depends on F099, F102.

Postgres/MySQL/SQLite use existing commitBatch transactions in bounded 250-row batches; standalone MongoDB uses one-document atomic insertRow calls. The Tables toolbar and shared CsvImportDialog provide exact-name mapping defaults, dry-run invalidation, coerced preview, and inserted/failed result reporting while hiding the action for unavailable targets. features.behavior: EXPLAIN viewer for the SQL editor (read-only-safe, a standard IDE capability): an Explain action runs the engine-appropriate plan statement for the current query - Postgres EXPLAIN (optionally ANALYZE behind an explicit toggle with a warning that ANALYZE executes the statement, and never for non-SELECT classifications), MySQL EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN FORMAT=TREE, SQLite EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN; MongoDB not-applicable (no SQL surface) - and renders the plan in a readable dedicated panel (text/tree; no graphical layout this slice). assertReadOnly already allows the EXPLAIN keyword, so read-only sessions get this too. Unit tests for the per-engine statement construction; e2e asserts a plan renders for a fixture query on one engine. features.evidence: Draft PR #138 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/138), pushed as 631510d. Added the optional DatabaseAdapter.explainQuery contract, authenticated POST /api/query/explain route, and normalized QueryPlanResult across PostgreSQL EXPLAIN (FORMAT TEXT), MySQL EXPLAIN FORMAT=TREE, and SQLite EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN; MongoDB is explicitly not applicable because it has no SQL editor surface. Every adapter retains its authoritative read-only backstop. PostgreSQL ANALYZE is a visibly warned opt-in, accepts only read-classified SQL, and runs inside a READ ONLY transaction. Live conformance found MySQL rejects DML planning inside START TRANSACTION READ ONLY, so Qyre limits MySQL Explain to read-classified SQL instead of weakening the guard; PostgreSQL and SQLite plain plans proved write-shaped SQL remains non-executing. The SQL Editor adds Explain/Analyze controls plus a dedicated resizable monospaced plan panel with loading, error, empty, classification, and analyzed states; changing SQL/engine or running a normal query clears stale output. Verified on Node 22 with the exact feature command (server 271 tests, UI 350 tests), live four-engine conformance, focused PostgreSQL E2E, pnpm verify:pr locally and through pre-push (34/34 package tasks, 11 smoke E2E passes, 29 full E2E passes), and both GitHub CI jobs passed.

features.behavior: A read-only Roles & grants viewer so users understand why affordances are hidden: Postgres shows pg_roles plus a grants summary for the current user, MySQL shows SHOW GRANTS/information_schema privileges (including granted roles), MongoDB shows rolesInfo/usersInfo where permitted, SQLite shows file-permission facts instead; strictly a viewer - no role management mutations anywhere in plan 0006. Surfaces through the admin namespace with a capability flag; degrades cleanly when the connected user may not read role catalogs. Depends on F092-F095.

The capability-driven Settings Access viewer covers disconnected, unsupported, capability-loading, data-loading, empty, degraded-notice, error, retry, and success states without engine-name branches or mutations. features.behavior: Permission-denied hardening across every mutating path: engine permission errors map to structured, friendly responses (which operation, which object, the likely missing grant) instead of raw engine text; a denial triggers a capabilities/permissions refetch so UI affordances converge with reality when grants change mid-session (the advisory-introspection principle in exec plan 0006); the event log records each denial. Conformance covers a denied insert/update/ddl per engine using the restricted fixtures with grants revoked mid-session where the engine allows. Depends on the write surfaces it protects - schedule after F117.

features.behavior: Close SUGGESTIONS.md S1: the F122 session token is currently served unauthenticated to any local requester - GET / (and the SPA fallback) returns index.html with window.__QYRE_TOKEN__ embedded (packages/server/src/plugins/static-web.ts), so any local process or other OS user can curl the port and gain full API access, contradicting SECURITY.md's 'stops any other local process/user' claim. Decide and implement: either harden the handout (e.g. one-time token mint on first page load, subsequent tokenless loads rejected) or explicitly document same-machine trust as an accepted limitation in docs/SECURITY.md so the claim matches the implementation. Either way SECURITY.md, the static-web plugin comment, and tests must end up consistent.
features.evidence: Reviewed the harden-vs-document tradeoff (SUGGESTIONS.md S1) and chose to document: closing the unauthenticated GET / token handout would need session-claim infrastructure (a cookie or one-time handshake) with real UX regressions for a single-developer local tool - page refresh, reopening a closed tab, and multiple tabs must all keep working with no separate login step. docs/SECURITY.md's bearer-token bullet now precisely scopes what the token defends (cross-origin/CSRF-shaped requests) and adds an explicit 'Accepted limitation' note; auth-guard.ts and static-web.ts's comments (which previously claimed the token stops 'any other local process/user') now match. `pnpm --filter @qyre/server test` (271 tests, unchanged - comment/doc-only) and `pnpm test:e2e` smoke suite (11 passed, including auth-token.spec.ts) both green on Node 22.

features.behavior: Close SUGGESTIONS.md S2 (+C2): with --verbose the export download URL's ?token=<session token> is logged verbatim by Fastify's request logging, writing the live bearer token into terminal output/captured logs. Add pino redaction (redact paths or a serializer) for the token query param when packages/cli builds the logger options, so verbose logs never contain the token while query-param auth keeps working. Cover with a server test asserting the logged request line masks the token.
features.evidence: Closed SUGGESTIONS.md S2/C2: added packages/server/src/services/log-redaction.ts (redactSensitiveQueryParams masks the export URL's ?token= query param; buildLoggerOptions normalizes every CreateServerOptions.logger form - true, {level}, false - into a Fastify logger config that always attaches the redacting req serializer) and wired it into createServer, so --verbose can no longer bypass it. New tests: log-redaction.test.ts (5 unit tests on the pure masking function) and app-logging.test.ts (3 integration tests against a captured pino stream, asserting a real request through /api/health?token=... never writes the live token while unrelated params and the non-verbose/no-logger path stay unchanged). pnpm --filter @qyre/server test (279 tests) and pnpm --filter @qyre/qyre test (46 tests, CLI unaffected) both green; full pnpm check:quiet (34/34 tasks) and check:state also green on Node 22.

features.behavior: Close SUGGESTIONS.md S3: describeError output (packages/server/src/services/connection-display.ts) flows unredacted into POST /api/connect 400 bodies, /api/health lastError, the EventLog, and the CLI's connect-failure message - driver-generated text (notably MongoDB URI parse errors) can echo connection-string fragments containing credentials. Apply a credential-masking pass (userinfo and credential-named query params anywhere in the string, same pattern family as redactConnectionString) to describeError output before it is returned, logged, or printed.
features.evidence: Closed SUGGESTIONS.md S3: added packages/server/src/services/connection-display.ts's redactErrorMessage() and applied it to every describeError() return path (Error, AggregateError unwrapping, and non-Error String() fallback) so a driver-generated error can never flow unredacted into POST /api/connect's 400 body, /api/health's lastError, the EventLog, or the CLI's connect-failure message. Masks a URL-shaped ://user:password@ fragment (password half only, mirroring @qyre/core's redactConnectionString) and any credential-named query param found anywhere in the text (same substring rule redactConnectionString uses), operating on free text that may only contain a connection string as a substring rather than text that must parse as one URL. New tests: userinfo redaction, query-param redaction, an ordinary message left untouched, AggregateError unwrapping still redacted, and a non-Error value's string form. pnpm --filter @qyre/server test (287 tests, 7 new) and @qyre/qyre test (46, CLI unaffected) both green; full pnpm check:quiet (34/34 tasks) also green on Node 22.

features.behavior: Close SUGGESTIONS.md S4: apps/web/src/features/connection/model/recent-targets.ts's SENSITIVE_PARAMETER regex full-matches bare names only, so compound credential params like sslpassword or access_token pass canPersistTarget and are persisted to localStorage, violating the 'persisted recent targets must be credential-free' rule. Switch to substring matching at least as strict as @qyre/core's CREDENTIAL_QUERY_PARAM_PATTERN and extend the unit tests with sslpassword/access_token/authSecret cases.
features.evidence: Closed SUGGESTIONS.md S4: apps/web/src/features/connection/model/recent-targets.ts's SENSITIVE_PARAMETER regex was anchored to the whole key (^...$), so a compound name like sslpassword (a real libpq param), access_token, or authSecret never matched and the target was judged safe to persist to localStorage, violating the 'persisted recent targets must be credential-free' rule. Dropped the anchors so every existing branch matches as a substring, at least as strict as @qyre/core's own CREDENTIAL_QUERY_PARAM_PATTERN (/password|pwd|secret|token/i) while keeping the two additional patterns (api key, credential) this check has always covered beyond core's set. New test cases cover sslpassword, access_token, authSecret, and tlsCertificateKeyFilePassword, plus a confirming case that an unrelated param still persists normally. pnpm --filter @qyre/web test (137 tests, 5 new assertions) green; full pnpm check:quiet (34/34 tasks) also green on Node 22.

features.evidence: Closed SUGGESTIONS.md S5: GET /api/files/content previously readFileSync'd the whole target with no size limit. Added readFilePreview() (packages/server/src/services/files.ts): stats first, reads in full at or under FILES_PREVIEW_MAX_BYTES (1 MiB, packages/core), otherwise reads only the first maxBytes via a bounded readSync into a fixed-size buffer, never loading the whole file. features.behavior: Close SUGGESTIONS.md V1: PATCH /api/tables/:schema/:table/ddl/columns/:column (packages/server/src/routes/schema-ddl.ts) runs rename then alter as two independent steps - when alter fails after rename succeeded, the rename silently persists while the route reports total failure, and a retry hits 'Unknown column'. Make the combined request atomic where the engine supports transactional DDL (Postgres, SQLite), or return a structured partial-success body ({ renamed, altered, error }) that EditColumnDialog renders honestly; MySQL (no transactional DDL) takes whichever path fits.

features.evidence: Closed SUGGESTIONS.md V1: added SchemaDdlApi.renameAndAlterColumn (one call, ColumnUpdateResult: { column, renamed, altered, alterError? }) per engine. Postgres: one client + BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK around both statements - any failure rolls back everything (verified live: a forced incompatible-cast alter after a real rename leaves the original column name intact). SQLite: both steps nested inside one db.transaction() (better-sqlite3 uses SAVEPOINTs for nested transaction functions, confirmed live) - same all-or-nothing guarantee around alterColumn's 12-step rebuild. MySQL: DDL auto-commits per statement, so no transaction can span two ALTER TABLE statements - genuinely can't be atomic; runs sequentially and returns { renamed: true, altered: false, alterError } instead of throwing when a post-rename alter fails (verified live against a real strict-mode cast failure). packages/server/src/routes/schema-ddl.ts's PATCH route now makes one combined call and returns the full result at 200, including the partial-outcome case (matching CSV import's precedent for a partial-success body over a special status code). apps/web's editColumn refreshes table metadata before surfacing an alterError as a thrown error, so a dialog retry after a MySQL partial success targets the now-current column name instead of the original bug's stale one. New tests: server route tests for the combined call and the partial-success response; live-DB driver integration tests on all three engines (rollback verification for Postgres/SQLite, partial-success verification for MySQL). pnpm --filter @qyre/server test (280), @qyre/postgres test (70), @qyre/sqlite test (50), @qyre/mysql test (60), @qyre/web test (134), and @qyre/ui test (350) all green; full pnpm check:quiet (34/34 tasks) also green on Node 22.

features.behavior: Close SUGGESTIONS.md V2: POST /api/mutations/commit validates staged ops via Promise.all(ops.map(resolveBatchOp)), firing one full getTable introspection per op even though a batch is almost always many ops against one table - 200 staged edits mean 200 concurrent identical introspection query sets before the transaction starts. Group ops by schema.table, introspect each table once, and validate every op against the shared metadata; behavior (including per-op validation failures aborting the whole commit) is unchanged.
features.evidence: Closed SUGGESTIONS.md V2: added resolveBatchOps() (packages/server/src/services/row-mutation-validation.ts) - groups staged ops by schema.table, introspects each distinct target exactly once via getTable, then resolves every op synchronously against the shared metadata (assertMutable + the matching resolve* helper, factored into a new resolveOneOp helper both entry points share). Ops keep their original relative order in the returned array (result.failedIndex and the route's own ops[] lookups both depend on it), and a validation failure on any op still throws before commitBatch is ever called - the reported failure is now deterministic (first array-order op with a problem) instead of whichever of N concurrent per-op promises happened to reject first. Removed the old per-op resolveBatchOp entry point since the route was its only caller and it's now fully superseded. New tests: shared-introspection call counting at both the service layer (single- and multi-table batches) and the route layer (a live HTTP request through the whole stack), plus a multi-op-failure ordering test. pnpm --filter @qyre/server test (294 tests) green; full pnpm check:quiet (34/34 tasks) also green on Node 22.

features.evidence: Closed SUGGESTIONS.md V3: added CSV_IMPORT_MAX_ERRORS (100, packages/core) and a small createErrorSink helper in packages/server/src/services/csv-import.ts - tracks the true failure count separately from the capped stored list, so failedRows in the response is never wrong even once the errors array itself stops growing. Every push site (row-coercion failures, MongoDB per-document rejections, a rolled-back SQL batch's per-row entries) goes through the sink. packages/ui's CsvImportReport shows 'Showing the first N of M errors.' whenever errors.length is less than failedRows. New tests: a 150-bad-row CSV asserting errors is capped at 100 while failedRows still reports 150 (server), and the notice appears/doesn't across capped, uncapped, and zero-error cases (ui). Updated one pre-existing test whose own 250-entry expectation was the exact unbounded behavior this closes. Real browser file-upload automation wasn't feasible with available tools (browsers block programmatic .files assignment on <input type=file>), so verification relied on integration tests exercising the real processCsvImport function against real CSV streams plus component tests using the exact CsvImportResult shape the server produces. pnpm --filter @qyre/server test (295 tests) and @qyre/ui test (365 tests) green; full pnpm check:quiet (34/34 tasks) also green on Node 22.

features.behavior: Close SUGGESTIONS.md V4: a nullable primary-key value (legal in SQLite non-INTEGER PKs) coerces to null in resolveKey and binds into 'pk = ?' in every SQL adapter, which never matches - the mutation reports matched 0 and the UI shows the misleading 'This row was already changed or removed.' Either generate IS NULL for null key values in the adapters' key clauses, or reject null key values at validation (row-mutation-validation.ts) with an explicit 'rows with a NULL primary key cannot be targeted' message; pick one and cover it with a SQLite-backed test.

features.behavior: Close SUGGESTIONS.md U2+U4+U5 (EditableCell/NewRowCell fixes, one slice since all live in the same two components): (1) text/number editors can never stage NULL or empty string - an empty draft silently cancels and the promised null button only exists for boolean/date widgets; render the null button for nullable text/number columns and make an empty draft stage '' explicitly; (2) the date/time/datetime editing branch has no cancel path - handle Escape (and blur) like handleTextKeyDown does; (3) numeric drafts round-trip through Number(), silently corrupting integers beyond 2^53 (SQLite safeIntegers / Postgres bigint arrive as strings) - keep the draft as a string when the parsed value is not a safe integer, or reject with a clear message. Per docs/product-specs/row-editing.md.
features.evidence: Closed SUGGESTIONS.md U2+U4+U5 in packages/ui/src/data-grid/editable-cell.tsx and new-row-cell.tsx. U2: added a null button to the nullable text/number editor (onMouseDown preventDefault so it doesn't blur-commit and unmount itself before its own click fires) and made an empty text draft commit '' explicitly instead of silently cancelling; an empty number draft still cancels (empty string isn't a valid number), with the null button as the explicit way to clear it. U4: added an Escape handler on the date/time/datetime editor's wrapping container (fires regardless of which internal DateTimeInput segment has focus) - no commit-on-blur counterpart, since DateTimeInput is a compound multi-input widget and Safari doesn't focus a <button> on click by default, making a naive blur check unable to distinguish a real blur from clicking the null button. U5: both components now reject a numeric draft whose integer value exceeds Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER instead of silently rounding it (SQLite safeIntegers/Postgres bigint deliver exact large values as strings precisely to avoid this) - red border, draft preserved, stays in edit mode. New unit tests: 9 in editable-cell, 2 in new-row-cell; all existing tests unaffected. Live-verified against a running Postgres preview (rebuilt @qyre/ui and @qyre/web): committed an explicit empty string via the text editor, confirmed the null button appears and commits null, and confirmed a bigint value beyond 2^53 gets the red-border rejection with the draft preserved rather than silently rounding. pnpm --filter @qyre/ui test (359 tests, 11 new) and @qyre/web test (136) green; full pnpm check:quiet (34/34 tasks) also green on Node 22.
